plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks topped with huge golden-yellow flower heads and dark, seed-packed centers, turning in unison toward the sun across fields and garden borders.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-July through late August, with some blooms lasting into September
plants.location: Temperate North America, Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not one flower but hundreds to thousands of tiny florets. The outer ray florets form the 'petals', and the inner disc florets each become a seed.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: Dense, arching plumes of tiny golden flowers light up meadows, roadsides and old fields, buzzing with bees, butterflies and beetles.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late July through August, continuing into early autumn
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, including the Ottawa region of Canada
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and carried by insects. The usual culprit is ragweed, which blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest of all proteas, with a bowl-shaped crown of silky-tipped pink bracts around a central cluster of true flowers. It is a showpiece of the Cape's fynbos.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter and spring, June to October, so late August is within the peak
plants.location: Western and Eastern Cape fynbos, South Africa (including Kirstenbosch gardens)
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower. Its lineage is ancient, and the genus name Protea honors the Greek sea god Proteus, who could change shape, a nod to the many forms in the family.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small tree that erupts into clouds of fluffy, fragrant golden pom-pom flowers that brighten the southern Australian bush at the end of winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Roughly July to October; August to October around Perth and in much of southeastern Australia
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including South Australia, Victoria and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the official first day of spring.
